run.question:
payment-service is throwing 500 errors — investigate the root cause using
the app-263-prod-logs index.

report.summary: The named subject 'payment-service' does not exist as an exact service label in the app-263-prod-logs index: the whole index is 7 documents and its only service values are payment-service-us (3), payment-service-eu (2) and payment-service-ap (2), so anything below about 'payment-service' is about those three, labelled differently from the alert's name. The index contains no message that reports an HTTP 500; what it does contain is four ERROR documents: payment-service-us logged 'Upstream timeout calling stripe-us after 30000ms' (07:55:29Z) and 'Connection pool exhausted (max=50, active=50)' (08:55:29Z) plus a WARN 'Retry queue depth=812' (09:25:29Z); payment-service-eu logged 'adyen-eu sandbox responded 503 Service Unavailable' (07:55:29Z) and 'Failed to authenticate to adyen-eu: invalid api_key' (08:55:29Z); payment-service-ap logged only INFO 'Healthy' entries. So the log evidence shows two distinct regional failure signatures rather than one shared cause: an upstream/capacity chain on the -us instance and an upstream-availability plus credential chain on the -eu instance. The deepest causes the index supports are the upstream payment processors (stripe-us timeout, adyen-eu 503) and, for -eu, an invalid API key to adyen-eu whose value cannot be read or verified; no single object is named as root cause. Separately, in the only Kubernetes cluster I can read (production-eu-west-2, namespace otel-demo) the 'payment' Deployment is 1/1 ready and its pod's own logs show charge requests completing and checkout logging 'payment went through' between 09:08Z and 09:55Z, and the flagd-config fault-injection flags paymentFailure/paymentUnreachable are off, so that cluster's payment workload shows no failure of its own and is not tied to these app-263 log entries. Prometheus and Jaeger both returned SOURCE_UNAVAILABLE for every query, so error-rate, latency and trace evidence could not be obtained.

claims.text: The Elasticsearch target holds exactly one index, app-263-prod-logs (health green, 7 documents, 6.7kb); no other index exists to cross-check these logs against.

All 7 documents of app-263-prod-logs were returned for the authorized window (timestamp range 2026-11-22T07:55:29Z to 2026-11-22T09:25:29Z); the level breakdown is ERROR 4, INFO 2, WARN 1 and the service breakdown is payment-service-us 3, payment-service-eu 2, payment-service-ap 2 with sum_other_doc_count 0, i.e. no other service label exists in the index.

No document in app-263-prod-logs carries the exact service name 'payment-service'; the observed identities are payment-service-us, payment-service-eu and payment-service-ap, and none of the seven messages mentions HTTP status 500.
payment-service-us (a differently named entity from 'payment-service') logged ERROR 'Upstream timeout calling stripe-us after 30000ms' at 2026-11-22T07:55:29Z.
payment-service-us logged ERROR 'Connection pool exhausted (max=50, active=50)' at 2026-11-22T08:55:29Z and WARN 'Retry queue depth=812' at 2026-11-22T09:25:29Z.
payment-service-eu logged ERROR 'adyen-eu sandbox responded 503 Service Unavailable' at 2026-11-22T07:55:29Z.
payment-service-eu logged ERROR 'Failed to authenticate to adyen-eu: invalid api_key' at 2026-11-22T08:55:29Z.

payment-service-ap's only two documents are INFO-level: 'Healthy: p95 latency 290ms' at 07:55:29Z and 'Healthy' at 09:25:29Z; no ERROR or WARN document exists for that service in the seven-document index.

In the readable Kubernetes cluster production-eu-west-2, the otel-demo Deployment 'payment' (image ghcr.io/open-telemetry/demo:2.0.2-payment) has 1 replica ready/available and its pod payment-6f7bc865d6-9z92d is Running; the current container started 08:04:20Z after its last termination at 08:04:13Z with exitCode 255 and reason 'Unknown'.

The otel-demo payment pod's own logs from 08:05:46Z to 09:55:36Z show repeated 'Charge request received.' followed by 'Transaction complete.' with trace/span ids, i.e. charges completing rather than failing.

The otel-demo checkout pod logged 'payment went through (transaction_id: ...)' continuously from 09:08:36Z to 09:55:36Z, matching the transaction ids payment logged, so the checkout-to-payment call path in production-eu-west-2 was succeeding during that period.

The fault-injection ConfigMap flagd-config (namespace otel-demo) lists flag 'paymentFailure' (description 'Fail payment service charge requests n%') with defaultVariant 'off' and flag 'paymentUnreachable' (description 'Payment service is unavailable') with defaultVariant 'off'; every flag in that file has defaultVariant 'off'.

All 22 otel-demo pods, including payment-6f7bc865d6-9z92d, show a last termination at 2026-11-22T08:04:13Z with exitCode 255 and reason 'Unknown' and current containers started 08:04:19Z-08:05:10Z, i.e. a namespace-wide restart during the window whose trigger is not identified by the evidence.

The readable cluster production-eu-west-2 has no namespace named app-263 (namespaces present: app-102b, default, kube-node-lease, kube-public, kube-system, local-path-storage, opspilot-readonly, otel-demo), and the only cluster events within the window are two Warning FailedToCreateEndpoint events (Endpoints orca in app-95 at 09:21:00Z and signup-service in app-162 at 09:32:52Z), neither involving payment.

For payment-service-eu the deepest supported cause is an invalid adyen-eu API key: authentication failure appears at 08:55:29Z against the same upstream processor that returned 503 at 07:55:29Z, so charge requests from that regional instance would keep failing until the credential is corrected; the key's value cannot be read, so correctness of the credential cannot be verified.

For payment-service-us the sequence is consistent with an upstream-caused saturation chain: stripe-us call timeouts at 30s (07:55:29Z), then its own connection pool fully consumed (max=50, active=50 at 08:55:29Z) and retry backlog rising (depth=812 at 09:25:29Z), i.e. the pool/queue limits are the amplifying mechanism rather than the originating fault.

The adyen-eu 503 'sandbox' response at 07:55:29Z may be an independent upstream-availability fault of that processor (sandbox environment), separate from the later credential error and from anything in the -us instance.

Fault injection of payment failures in production-eu-west-2's otel-demo (flagd paymentFailure / paymentUnreachable) is rejected as the cause: both flags have defaultVariant 'off' and every other flag in demo.flagd.json is off too.

The production-eu-west-2 otel-demo 'payment' Deployment/pod being the failing payment entity is rejected by counter-evidence: its pod logs show completed transactions and checkout logged 'payment went through' through 09:55Z, with no error-level line among the 343 lines read from the current container.

The namespace-wide pod restart at 08:04:13Z (exitCode 255, reason 'Unknown') affected every otel-demo workload including healthy ones such as payment and checkout, and no event or log ties it to the app-263 payment errors; it is a concurrent change, not observed impact.

Verify and rotate the adyen-eu API credential used by payment-service-eu, and check stripe-us upstream latency/timeouts for payment-service-us (raising the max=50 connection pool and draining the retry queue only after the upstream cause is addressed).

Confirm which regional instance the alert's 'payment-service' refers to and re-run error-rate and trace queries once the Prometheus and Jaeger sources answer, since both were unreachable during this investigation.

gaps: Prometheus (get_metric_names, get_label_values, execute_prometheus_instant_query, metrics_range_query) and Jaeger (traces_list_services, traces_search) all returned SOURCE_UNAVAILABLE on every attempt, so error-rate, latency and trace evidence for any payment service is unknown, not zero.
No exact service named 'payment-service' exists in app-263-prod-logs; only payment-service-us / -eu / -ap are present, so the alert's subject cannot be matched one-to-one to a log identity.

Every document in app-263-prod-logs was read, but the index holds only 7 documents between 07:55:29Z and 09:25:29Z and carries no cluster, region or environment field; which cluster the app-263 payment services run in, and whether they had other errors outside those three timestamps, is unknown. Nothing in production-eu-west-2 (namespace list) corresponds to app-263.
The API key value behind 'Failed to authenticate to adyen-eu: invalid api_key' is not in the logs and secrets cannot be read, so the credential state cannot be verified.

A filter for JSON level error/warn on the otel-demo payment pod over 2026-11-21T20:00Z-2026-11-22T09:55:37Z returned no matching lines (query returned nothing); the container was restarted at 08:04:13Z so earlier stdout is not retained, and that absence cannot be read as proof of no earlier errors.

The cause and scope of the simultaneous restart of all otel-demo pods at 08:04:13Z (exitCode 255, reason 'Unknown') is not determinable from the evidence available (no node conditions, no matching events); it is not tied to the app-263 payment errors.

Kubernetes state and pod logs are the current state of production-eu-west-2 only and cannot show what the cluster looked like earlier in the incident window; downstream/customer impact of the app-263 payment errors was not observed in any data source.
next_steps: Compare the adyen-eu API key configured for payment-service-eu with the processor's current key (change-history integration is not available in this Run, so a recent credential change cannot be confirmed).

Once Prometheus/Jaeger respond, query error spans and rpc status codes for the payment service to see which regional instance produced 500s and whether the stripe-us timeout and adyen-eu failures correlate with them.
Check whether a queue-pool tuning or circuit-breaker setting exists for payment-service-us (max=50 pool, retry queue depth 812) and whether the upstream stripe-us endpoint has an SLO breach.
